Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 93, verses 1–11:

Explanation of the words:

"By the morning brightness" (wal-duha): that is, the first part of the day, from the rising of the sun until it is a spear's length high, up to the zenith (al-zawal).

"And by the night when it is still" (wal-layli idha saja): it covers the inhabited world with its darkness, and it becomes calm, so people settle down and incline to rest.

"Your Lord has not forsaken you" (ma wadda'aka): that is, He has not left you nor abandoned you.

"Nor has He detested you" (wa ma qala): that is, He has not hated you.

"Did He not find you an orphan" (alam yajidka yatiman): that is, one who had lost his father, for his father died before he was born.

"And give you shelter" (fa-awa): that is, He sheltered you by placing you under the care of your uncle Abu Talib.

"And find you lost" (wa wajadaka dallan): that is, you did not know religion or guidance.

"And find you in need" (wa wajadaka a'ilan): that is, poor.

"And enrich you" (fa-aghna): that is, with contentment, and with what was made easy for you of the wealth of Khadijah and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq.

"So do not oppress" (fa-la taqhar): that is, do not humiliate him nor take his wealth.

"So do not repel" (fa-la tanhar): that is, do not rebuke him with harshness or the like.

"And as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it" (wa amma bini'mati rabbika fa-haddith): that is, mention what Allah the Exalted has bestowed upon you, in gratitude to Him for that.

Explanation of the verses:

The words of the Exalted, ﴿By the morning brightness and by the night when it is still. Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾ — this is an oath made by Allah the Exalted to His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, swearing to him that He has neither left him nor hated him. The reason was that revelation was delayed from him for some days. When the polytheists saw this, they rejoiced and taunted him, and a woman came and said: "I think your devil has only forsaken you." The Prophet ﷺ was saddened by this, so Allah sent down Surah al-Duha, swearing to him by the morning brightness, which is the first part of the day from the rising of the sun until it is a spear's length high, up to shortly before the zenith, and by the night when it is still, that is, when it covers the inhabited world with its darkness, and it becomes calm, so people settle down and incline to rest in it. ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you﴾, O Muhammad, that is, He has not left you. ﴿Nor has He detested you﴾, that is, He has not hated you. ﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the first﴾, that is, than this world, because of what Allah has prepared for you there of great dominion and everlasting great bounty. ﴿And your Lord will give you, and you will be satisfied﴾, from His abundant favors: in this world, the perfection of the religion and the manifestation of the matter; and in the Hereafter, intercession, that none of his community who are people of monotheism remain in the Fire, the Wasilah, and the lofty rank that belongs to no one other than him.

The words of the Exalted, ﴿Did He not find you an orphan and give you shelter? And find you lost and guide you? And find you in need and enrich you?﴾ — these are three favors of Allah upon His Messenger, which He bestowed upon him and reminded him of, so that he would be certain that Allah is with him and for him, that He has not left him and will not leave him, and so that the rejoicing of the polytheists at the delay and postponement of revelation for a few days would end. The first favor: the Prophet's ﷺ father died shortly after his birth, and his mother died soon after his weaning, so his Lord gave him shelter by placing him under the care of his uncle Abu Talib, who became a compassionate father and a noble uncle to him, and a firm fortress for him. He did not abandon his support and defense until his death. The second favor: the favor of knowledge and guidance. He ﷺ lived in Makkah like one of its men, knowing neither knowledge nor law, though he was protected from committing any sin or perpetrating any error. Yet he did not know faith, Islam, or the law, as the Exalted said: ﴿You did not know what the Book was, nor faith﴾ [al-Shura: 52]. The third favor: His bestowal upon him of richness after need. His father died and left nothing more than a slave-girl, who was Barakah, Umm Ayman, and a few camels, so Allah enriched him with the richness of contentment, and he never stretched out his hand to anyone. He used to say: "Richness is not in having many possessions, but richness is the richness of the soul." These are three divine favors, and how great they are. A favor calls for gratitude, and Allah gives more to the grateful. From here Allah the Exalted guided His Messenger to thank for these blessings so that He would increase them for him. So He said: ﴿As for the orphan, do not oppress him﴾, do not oppress him by taking his wealth, humiliating him, or harming him, remembering Allah's care for you during your orphanhood. ﴿As for the one who asks﴾, who is the poor, needy person in want who asks you for what will meet his need: give him what you find, whether a gift or a refusal with a kind word that soothes his heart and eases the pain of his soul, and do not repel him with harsh rebuke or unkind speech, remembering the need you were in and the poverty you felt. ﴿As for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it﴾, that is, thank for the blessing of faith, goodness, revelation, knowledge, and the Criterion, and that is done by speaking of them, by conveying, teaching, educating, and guiding. That is its thanks, and Allah loves the grateful. Thus did Allah, majestic in His majesty, discipline His Messenger and His beloved friend, and He perfected his discipline and made it good.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The world is never free of turbidity, and the Mighty God has spoken the truth: ﴿Indeed We have created man in hardship﴾ [al-Balad: 4].

2- Explanation of the exalted station of Muhammad and the nobility of his rank.

3- The legitimacy of reminding oneself of blessings and afflictions, to move the servant toward patience and gratitude.

4- The obligation to thank for blessings by spending them in pleasing the Bestower, Mighty and Majestic.

5- Affirmation of the meaning of the hadith: "When Allah bestows a blessing upon a servant, He loves to see its effect upon him."

Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you﴾ — this is an oath made by Allah the Exalted to His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, swearing to him that He has neither left him nor hated him. The reason was that revelation was delayed from him for some days. When the polytheists saw this, they rejoiced and taunted him, and a woman came and said: "I think your devil has only forsaken you." The Prophet ﷺ was saddened by this, so Allah sent down Surah al-Duha, swearing to him by the morning brightness, which is the first part of the day from the rising of the sun until it is a spear's length high, up to shortly before the zenith, and by the night when it is still, that is, when it covers the inhabited world with its darkness, and it becomes calm, so people settle down and incline to rest in it. ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you﴾, O Muhammad, that is, He has not left you. ﴿Nor has He detested you﴾, that is, He has not hated you. ﴿And the Hereafter is better for you than the first﴾, that is, than this world, because of what Allah has prepared for you there of great dominion and everlasting great bounty. ﴿And your Lord will give you, and you will be satisfied﴾, from His abundant favors: in this world, the perfection of the religion and the manifestation of the matter; and in the Hereafter, intercession, that none of his community who are people of monotheism remain in the Fire, the Wasilah, and the lofty rank that belongs to no one other than him.

The words of the Exalted, ﴿Did He not find you an orphan and give you shelter? And find you lost and guide you? And find you in need and enrich you?﴾ — these are three favors of Allah upon His Messenger, which He bestowed upon him and reminded him of, so that he would be certain that Allah is with him and for him, that He has not left him and will not leave him, and so that the rejoicing of the polytheists at the delay and postponement of revelation for a few days would end. The first favor: the Prophet's ﷺ father died shortly after his birth, and his mother died soon after his weaning, so his Lord gave him shelter by placing him under the care of his uncle Abu Talib, who became a compassionate father and a noble uncle to him, and a firm fortress for him. He did not abandon his support and defense until his death. The second favor: the favor of knowledge and guidance. He ﷺ lived in Makkah like one of its men, knowing neither knowledge nor law, though he was protected from committing any sin or perpetrating any error. Yet he did not know faith, Islam, or the law, as the Exalted said: ﴿You did not know what the Book was, nor faith﴾ [al-Shura: 52]. The third favor: His bestowal upon him of richness after need. His father died and left nothing more than a slave-girl, who was Barakah, Umm Ayman, and a few camels, so Allah enriched him with the richness of contentment, and he never stretched out his hand to anyone. He used to say: "Richness is not in having many possessions, but richness is the richness of the soul." These are three divine favors, and how great they are. A favor calls for gratitude, and Allah gives more to the grateful. From here Allah the Exalted guided His Messenger to thank for these blessings so that He would increase them for him. So He said: ﴿As for the orphan, do not oppress him﴾, do not oppress him by taking his wealth, humiliating him, or harming him, remembering Allah's care for you during your orphanhood. ﴿As for the one who asks﴾, who is the poor, needy person in want who asks you for what will meet his need: give him what you find, whether a gift or a refusal with a kind word that soothes his heart and eases the pain of his soul, and do not repel him with harsh rebuke or unkind speech, remembering the need you were in and the poverty you felt. ﴿As for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it﴾, that is, thank for the blessing of faith, goodness, revelation, knowledge, and the Criterion, and that is done by speaking of them, by conveying, teaching, educating, and guiding. That is its thanks, and Allah loves the grateful. Thus did Allah, majestic in His majesty, discipline His Messenger and His beloved friend, and He perfected his discipline and made it good.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The world is never free of turbidity, and the Mighty God has spoken the truth: ﴿Indeed We have created man in hardship﴾ [al-Balad: 4].

2- Explanation of the exalted station of Muhammad and the nobility of his rank.

3- The legitimacy of reminding oneself of blessings and afflictions, to move the servant toward patience and gratitude.

4- The obligation to thank for blessings by spending them in pleasing the Bestower, Mighty and Majestic.

5- Affirmation of the meaning of the hadith: "When Allah bestows a blessing upon a servant, He loves to see its effect upon him."

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 93, verses 1–11:

Explanation of the words:

"By the morning brightness" (wal-duha): that is, the first part of the day, from the rising of the sun until it is a spear's length high, up to the zenith (al-zawal).

"And by the night when it is still" (wal-layli idha saja): it covers the inhabited world with its darkness, and it becomes calm, so people settle down and incline to rest.

"Your Lord has not forsaken you" (ma wadda'aka): that is, He has not left you nor abandoned you.

"Nor has He detested you" (wa ma qala): that is, He has not hated you.

"Did He not find you an orphan" (alam yajidka yatiman): that is, one who had lost his father, for his father died before he was born.

"And give you shelter" (fa-awa): that is, He sheltered you by placing you under the care of your uncle Abu Talib.

"And find you lost" (wa wajadaka dallan): that is, you did not know religion or guidance.

"And find you in need" (wa wajadaka a'ilan): that is, poor.

"And enrich you" (fa-aghna): that is, with contentment, and with what was made easy for you of the wealth of Khadijah and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq.

"So do not oppress" (fa-la taqhar): that is, do not humiliate him nor take his wealth.

"So do not repel" (fa-la tanhar): that is, do not rebuke him with harshness or the like.

"And as for the blessing of your Lord, proclaim it" (wa amma bini'mati rabbika fa-haddith): that is, mention what Allah the Exalted has bestowed upon you, in gratitude to Him for that.
